one_line.text: Business writer, case developer, and former Duke social-entrepreneurship fellow who turns research and organisational cases into practical frameworks.

biography.text: Heath earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas Plan II programme and an MBA from Harvard Business School. He worked as a researcher and case writer at Harvard Business School, co-founded the educational publisher Thinkwell, and founded the Change Academy while affiliated with Duke's Center for the Advancement of Social Entrepreneurship.

background.text: His work combines reporting, cases, interviews, and behavioural research. With Chip Heath he wrote Made to Stick, Switch, Decisive, and The Power of Moments; his later solo work includes Upstream, Reset, and a podcast about different occupations.

expertise.text: Dan Heath's strongest direct expertise is explaining ideas, developing teaching cases, entrepreneurship education, publishing, and practical organisational change. He is not presented as an experimental psychologist; the scientific authority in the books comes from the research they interpret, not from his biography.

perspective_and_limits.text: His case-writing skill produces vivid, usable examples but selects successes after their outcomes are known. Readers should treat the cases as pattern illustrations and test interventions locally, especially when designed moments involve vulnerable people, employee labour, or commercial persuasion.
